name: The Opal MCP tool index -- every Opal data property answerable in Claude from ONE catalog: a discover family, purpose-built tools per property (portal, Schwab, Black Diamond, Orion, Eclipse, SmartX, ETFs), a typed fallback query, and on-demand history and market data
description: Commissioned by Andrew-direct 2026-09-17 at the 4.0.0_SA_CRO terminal, his words carried verbatim in the brief: 'I need you to essentially scope out how we could expand the tool index in the Opal MCP Server endpoint to address each of these properties. The issue with the official plugins is that they are very poorly indexed, and I don't want us to have that problem, so I'd like to develop a system for keeping this largely in AWS (on-demand functions secondary, but we should explore them), whereby each data segment (most of it is in opal-data-assets silver parquets, portal data being in the consumed tables from opal-data-portal-v2) is thoughtfully analyzed and we create tool calls for common queries.' His five card answers, verbatim: '1.) Refer to LGIC naming, there should be convention there to go off of. 2.) Versioned in S3 works. 3.) I would put it under D9 Opal Workflows. 4.) Opal Staff only, but we'll be beta testing it one at a time. 5.) There are precomputed tables for the Portal that we're already pointing at, pretty much everythng we're pointing at in aws is precomputed tables. With that said, yes we are focusing on live queries particularly for the opal-data-assets tables'. The shape: ONE catalog (extending app/refs/DATA_CATALOG.yaml, never a second), versioned in S3 at a builder-named address; a discover family loaded every session; per-property analysis before that property's tools are cut; a typed query (never raw SQL) as the safe fallback; one fenced read role per property; every tool classified before it ships.

PORTAL READS PRECOMPUTED, SILVER QUERIED LIVE -- his answer 5, which is also FWD-2's mechanism: Claude and the portal read the same tables, so they cannot disagree.

TOOL NAMES FOLLOW THE LGIC CANON -- his answer 1 ('Refer to LGIC naming'). The brief reads it as {system}_{function}[_{qualifier}] with scope as an explicit argument; whether the schema GRADES tool names is 1.0.0_SA_CTO's bump call at L4.
